overview: From 2025-10-01 to 2025-11-01, Sendo-labs/plugin-sendo-chat had 0 new PRs (0 merged), 0 new issues, and 1 active contributors.

topContributors.summary: standujar: Led the foundational development across the Sendo-labs ecosystem, establishing several core components from scratch. They were instrumental in creating new plugins, including the initial implementation of the Sendo Worker (`plugin-sendo-worker#1`, +13k lines) and migrating the Sendo Analyser (`plugin-sendo-analyser#1`, +17k lines). Standujar also added a major X social scoring feature (`leaderboard#9`) and established a comprehensive test infrastructure for the worker plugin (`plugin-sendo-worker#2`). Their work demonstrates a primary focus on feature development, project configuration, and building out test suites.

Neysixx: This month, Neysixx drove a massive foundational effort on the `Sendo-labs/frontend` repository, merging 15 PRs focused on architecture and new capabilities. They initiated this with a monumental refactor to establish the project structure and configurations (#1, +17867/-16129 lines), and immediately followed by implementing a core worker feature (#2, +8135/-3967 lines). Subsequent work introduced key functionalities such as a chat agent (#13), agent creation (#11), and a critical fix for build dependencies (#5). Overall, their activity shows a primary focus on large-scale refactoring and foundational feature development within the frontend codebase.

xdrkush: This month, xdrkush made foundational contributions across both the backend and frontend, notably establishing the `sendo-api` repository with a massive initial commit of over 21k lines (PR #1). They also implemented a significant "merge-analyzer" feature in the `frontend` repository (PR #17) and improved the API's stability by fixing buy/sell account logic (PRs #3, #4) and enhancing data analysis with rate limiting (PR #6). This activity, primarily composed of bug fixes and refactoring, demonstrates a strong focus on building and stabilizing core application functionality.

M4XGO: Focused on establishing and rolling out automated CI/CD infrastructure across several repositories this month. They initiated this effort by creating reusable workflows for release management in Sendo-labs/reusable-workflows#1 (+1005/-38 lines). Subsequently, M4XGO implemented these automated NPM publishing and deployment workflows across multiple plugins, including a significant setup in Sendo-labs/plugin-sendo-worker#3. This work, which consisted almost entirely of configuration file changes, demonstrates a clear focus on improving development operations and standardizing release processes.

0domart: This month, 0domart focused on implementing core functionality within the Sendo-labs/spotlight repository. They merged a single, substantial pull request (Sendo-labs/spotlight#1) which added over 1500 lines of code to complete the SOL transfer logic. This contribution demonstrates a primary focus on delivering new features along with their corresponding unit tests.

chainsona: This month's efforts were centered on a major feature implementation to reward contributors in the Sendo-labs/leaderboard-rewards repository. This work was delivered via a single, substantial pull request (#1) that introduced over 14,000 lines of code. The changes spanned 50 files, indicating a comprehensive effort that included not just new feature code but also tests, configuration, and documentation.

0xCanet: This month, 0xCanet's primary contribution was the initialization of the new `Sendo-labs/frontend` repository. They established the project's foundation through a single, substantial initial commit (PR #1), which added over 9,200 lines of code across 111 files. This foundational work indicates a focused effort on bootstrapping a new frontend application.

plvo: Focused on documentation within the Sendo-labs/Reports repository this month. Their main contribution was merging a pull request to add documentation for elizaos plugin reports (Sendo-labs/Reports#1), which added 146 lines of new content. All of their work this period was concentrated on documentation.

MonteCrypto999: Focused on developing a significant new feature to add referral fee support in the Jupiter plugin. This effort is contained within a single open pull request (Sendo-labs/plugin-jupiter#1), which represents a substantial body of work with +5,965 and -431 lines of code modified across 31 files. The code changes indicate a primary focus on feature work, supported by updates to configuration and tests.

Their sole contribution was merging a pull request (#2) to update the README file to English, making the project more accessible. All of their activity was concentrated on documentation.
